attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stating his position.

semantics.note: Faithfully restates current gains being smaller than the 2020-2022 gains. It is a present-tense observation, not a forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading (jumps between frontier generations, 2023-24 vs the GPT-3 to GPT-4 era) is an ordinary, fair reading. Whether reasoning models like o1 count as 'current gains' decides the result, and the speaker did not settle that.

evidence.note: Secondary summary of Bloomberg: Orion's gain was smaller than GPT-4's over its predecessor. Supports the claim for pretraining scale-up. Rests on unnamed sources.
OpenAI's own disclosure, Sept 2024: o1 went from 12% to 74% on AIME versus GPT-4o. That is a large jump on a major measure inside the period. Lab reports are allowed by the contract.
GPT-4 launch figures (bar exam, bottom 10% to top 10%). This is the baseline for the comparison, not evidence of the outcome.

reviews.rationale: Part holds: reporting says pretraining scale-up (Orion) gave a smaller jump than GPT-4 did. Part fails: o1 made a jump on hard math at least as large as the earlier ones. The support condition needs clearly smaller gains across the main measures, and that is not met. The contradiction condition is met only if reasoning models count. So the result is mixed.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Captures both parts: 18 months of incremental results, and Gemini 2 being only modestly better than 1.5. The 'tiny bit better' wording and the LiveBench figure are kept in the contract.

contract.note: Splitting the claim into a Gemini part and an 18-month part, and comparing 2.0 Flash with 1.5 Pro as he appears to, is a fair plain reading. 'Modest' and 'incremental' have no threshold, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Google's launch post says 2.0 Flash beats 1.5 Pro on key benchmarks but gives no size. It is a company disclosure.
Secondary reproduction of launch figures: MMLU-Pro 76.4 vs 75.8 for 1.5 Pro, a tiny gain consistent with 'modestly better'.
Same source: HiddenMath 63 vs 52 for 1.5 Pro, an 11-point gain. That is more than 'a tiny bit' on this measure.
o1's AIME jump from 12% to 74% (Sept 2024) falls inside the 18-month window. It is a large jump, not an incremental one. Company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: Gemini part: compared with 1.5 Pro, gains are small on MMLU-Pro, MATH and GPQA, which supports 'modestly better'. They are larger on HiddenMath and Natural2Code. The 34.3 figure is unverified. The 18-month part is contradicted by o1's large jump on AIME. Part (a) largely holds and part (b) fails.
